## Summary

Fujitsu is a Japanese IT company established on 20 June 1935 as a spin-off of Fuji Electric, headquartered in Kawasaki, Kanagawa, listed on the Tokyo and Nagoya stock exchanges, with the Furukawa Group named as its parent [1]. Its hardware is mainly personal and enterprise computing, networking equipment and storage, it has built mobile phones such as the NTT DoCoMo F-10A, and it delivered 5G telecom equipment to NTT Docomo in 2019 [1]. Its PC business was spun off in 2017 into Fujitsu Client Computing, a joint venture in which Lenovo holds 51 percent and Fujitsu 44 percent [1].

The registry holds 21 MA-L blocks as FUJITSU LIMITED and three as Fujitsu Limited, all at Kawasaki addresses [2]. Fujitsu Client Computing Limited, Fujitsu Technology Solutions GmbH and the other Fujitsu subsidiaries are separate registry names and are not folded in here [2]. A MAC in one of these blocks may be a Fujitsu PC, server, phone or network element; which one is not documented in the sources consulted [1].

No radios, silicon, FCC grantee codes or advisories are listed: the FCC ID databases refused the session that wrote this entry and no Fujitsu security advisory was consulted, so nothing is filled in from memory. Randomization is the host operating system's behaviour and is unknown here.
